item.title: Big hiccup! Scotch whisky faces 162.5% duty despite India-UK trade deal: Why shipments are stuck and what went wrong
item.description: India's 162.5% effective duty on bulk Scotch imports has left over 80 shipping containers stuck at ports, triggering a dispute under the India-UK trade pact. Liquor companies face higher costs and working capital pressure as they seek the agreed 75% tariff.
item.dc:creator: Prabhakar Jha
item.content:encoded: Amid a raging dispute over the India-UK trade pact, India is now imposing an effective duty of 162.5% on bulk Scotch whisky imports, Reuters reported. The development has left thousands of litres of whisky stuck at Indian ports and putting liquor companies in a difficult position despite a trade agreement that was expected to lower import costs.The India-UK trade agreement, which came into effect in July, reduced tariffs on Scotch whisky from 150% to 75%. The move was expected to benefit companies such as Diageo and Pernod Ricard, which import Scotch in bulk and blend it with other spirits to manufacture popular whisky brands for India's $65 billion liquor market.Why is India imposing 162.5% duty on bulk Scotch imports?The disagreement centres on the customs classification of bulk Scotch whisky and whether it qualifies for the tariff concessions under the India-UK trade agreement.Under the pact, tariffs on Scotch whisky imports were reduced from 150% to 75%. However, Indian investigators have argued that bulk Scotch concentrates should be classified differently from finished whisky.According to Reuters, investigators contend that since May, these imports have come under a newly created customs category called "compound alcoholic preparations", which attracts a 150% tariff.An additional consumption tax takes the effective duty to 162.5%.Indian authorities have argued that bulk Scotch is merely a raw material used to manufacture blended whisky and other alcoholic beverages, and therefore does not qualify for the reduced tariff under the trade agreement.Liquor companies, however, disagree with this interpretation. Pernod Ricard, Diageo and several Indian manufacturers believe all Scotch imports, whether bottled or brought in bulk, should attract the concessional 75% tariff under the pact.Why are Scotch whisky shipments stuck at Indian ports?The customs classification dispute has left thousands of litres of bulk Scotch in more than 80 shipping containers belonging to Pernod Ricard, Diageo and Bacardi stuck at Indian ports.While investigations continue, companies can seek provisional release of their consignments by paying duty equivalent to 75% of the goods' value upfront and covering the remaining amount through bank guarantees, Reuters reported, citing sources familiar with the matter.Pernod Ricard and Diageo have moved to arrange bank guarantees and other funding to secure the release of their blocked consignments and keep business operations running. Bacardi, meanwhile, was still considering its next steps.The arrangement is creating additional pressure on companies' working capital. Smaller liquor manufacturers could face greater difficulties in arranging bank guarantees because they may need to provide collateral. These guarantees also have to be reported as contingent liabilities.Why do Indian whisky makers need bulk Scotch?Bulk Scotch imports play an important role in India's whisky industry, as they are used by domestic manufacturers to produce Indian-Made Foreign Liquor (IMFL) whisky.Around 80% of Scotch whisky imports from Britain by volume arrive in bulk, according to Reuters. Most of these imports are used to manufacture blended whisky by mixing Scotch with other spirits and ingredients.These products are sold at considerably lower prices than fully imported Scotch brands such as Chivas Regal and Johnnie Walker.This makes the tariff dispute significant for Indian liquor manufacturers as well as international whisky companies. A prolonged disruption in bulk Scotch supplies could affect production requirements and increase costs for manufacturers that depend on these imports.How is the UK responding to the dispute?The UK government has repeatedly said it is working with New Delhi to resolve the disagreement and ensure British businesses can export under the tariffs agreed in the trade deal.A UK government spokesperson told Reuters that ministers were "urgently working with the government of India to resolve this issue to ensure UK businesses can export under the tariffs agreed in the trade deal".The Scotch Whisky Association has estimated that Scotch exports to India stood at $335 million in 2024 and forecast that the trade agreement could increase exports by $1.34 billion over five years.

item.title: Trump, Putin and Xi to hold historic trilateral meeting in China: What's on the agenda and why it matters
item.description: US President Donald Trump met Russian President Vladimir Putin in China ahead of talks with Xi Jinping. The proposed trilateral meeting is expected to cover nuclear disarmament, Iran, global trade and the Russia-Ukraine war.
item.dc:creator: Prabhakar Jha
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump on Thursday met his Russian counterpart, Vladimir Putin, in China's Shenzhen on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit, Reuters reported. It was their first in-person meeting in more than a year."We've had a great relationship for many years. We know each other for a long time, and I think a lot of wonderful things can come out of this, or at least start. But I think they'll come out of this," Trump told Putin, according to Reuters. "He's my friend," he added.The meeting comes ahead of Trump's talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping and a proposed trilateral meeting involving the three leaders.Earlier, Trump had described the proposed trilateral meeting as an opportunity to explore areas of cooperation among the three major powers."And here in China, I look forward to a historic trilateral meeting with President Xi and President Putin later today to discuss more opportunities for all three. So, we look forward to that, very much forward to that," he had said earlier.What is on the agenda of the trilateral meeting?While no official announcement has been made on the agenda of the proposed trilateral meeting, discussions are expected to cover several issues, including nuclear disarmament, the Iran war, global trade and the Russia-Ukraine war.The leaders could also discuss supply chain security, economic cooperation, artificial intelligence, digital infrastructure and technology governance."He [Trump] will discuss the reduction of nuclear weapons in the world, whose proliferation President Trump believes is very dangerous," Olivia Wales, a White House spokeswoman, told reporters during a briefing call, according to CNBC.White House officials have also said that Trump is not expected to raise the Russia-Ukraine war during the meeting. However, Trump has suggested that he could bring up the issue, Reuters reported.Speaking to Fox News, Trump said he would not seek help from Russia and China to bring the Iran conflict to an end.Xi receives Trump at airportEarlier on Wednesday, Chinese President Xi Jinping welcomed Trump at Shenzhen airport, the first time he has personally received a visiting leader at the airport since becoming president. The two leaders also shared a brief hug.The meeting in China also comes days after a major controversy erupted in US after an alleged Chinese spy "honey trapped" former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. The fall out of the affair resulted in Huang's exit from the company and tighter US control over the export of advance American-made semiconductors.
